To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nanoclusters decorated Ru, Co, and N codoped porous carbon catalysts are successfully prepared with bimmetallic zeolite framework as the precursor.
the Ru pCo@N C catalyst with low Ru loading of only 3.13% exhibits impressive HER performance in 1 M alkaline solution.

the Ru pCo@N C catalyst exhibits excellent electrocatalysis for HER, with a low overpotential of only about 30 mV to reach 10 mA cm, a Tafel slope of 32.1mV dec 1, and superior stability for 20 h continuous operation with a commercial Pt/C catalyst.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a low Ru loading electrocatalyst for hydrogen evolution reaction with excellent electrochemical properties.
a new strategy for designing high performance electrocatalysts by combining the advantages of different materials.

the design and development of highly efficient and durable electrocaticlysts for hydrogen evolution reaction, and the results provide an economical, efficient, and durable electroatalyst for practical applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bimetallic ZnCo ZIF derived Co/N codoped porous carbon supported Ru catalyst with low Ru content can be a promising candidate for practical HER application.
Ru pCo@ NC is a promising and economical electrocatalyst for practical application of water splitting.
Ru pCo@N C catalyst with a low loading of 3 wt% Ru is an economical, powerful, highly efficient, and durable catalyst for HER.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ZIF precursor derived porous carbon support and Ru pCo@N codoped active species are beneficial to enhance the HER catalytic activity and durability.
a novel strategy to design and prepare Ru pCo@Nc with high activity, durability, and low Ru content, which is a great potential to replace the commercial Pt/C for HER.
the bimetallic ZnCo ZIF is a promising precursor to prepare high performance HER electrocatalysts with low Ru loading.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bimetallic ZF derived Ru pCo@N codoped carbon is an excellent electrocatalyst for HER with high activity, low cost, and long term durability.
the Ru pCo@N C electrocatalysts can be a promising and competitive candidate for HER in alkaline electrolyte.
bimetallic ZI F derived Co/N Codoped porous carbon supported ruthenium catalysts are promising for highly efficient HER electrocatalysts.
